performers.role: der Koloss, in dem eine ganze Stadt arbeitet

residentHome: Kanzel eines riesigen Mechs, Rohre, Rohrpost, Bordsprechanlage
structure: the pilot behind the colossus' eyes finds the joysticks are not connected; each organ states its card and the pilot resolves it into an everyday target (smartwatch, breathing coach, seminar, boss, podcast); the memo makes him the press secretary; the outro widens the picture to a whole city of pilots (human folly) and invites play at the table
synopsis: A spoken-word number from a card deck that describes the human body as a city. It is performed by a giant walking machine, speaking as the pilot in its own cockpit, for whoever happens to be there.
bestOfReason: Hook 1: the body runs the civilization while you are busy.
Departments 5, 7, 10, 9, 28: each organ's claim resolved into an everyday target (watch, coach, seminar, Friday, streaming).
Security 11, 19: memory and friendly fire, resolved as the company that fires the whistleblower.
Medicine knows that move 21, 23, 24, 30: looking beats the book; nobody wants to hear it was their own hands; the meeting; the podcast.
Perception 26: guessing to fill the gap, also how we read the news.
Turn 6: the memo - press secretary, not president.

songLineChanges.songLine: The decision was already underway five hundred milliseconds before you made it.
The Lungs: seventy square meters folded into your chest.
Eighty percent of the phone calls go up to the brain.

beats: I'm the pilot of this colossus. Top floor, behind the eyes: two joysticks, a wall of blinking screens, a very comfortable chair.
For forty years I thought I was steering. Then I opened the floor panel. The joysticks aren't connected to anything.

beats.text: The City Inside has been running the civilization while you were busy with other things.
beats.post: My other things: a step counter.

beats.pre: Every morning my watch sends me a trophy for my resting pulse.
beats.text: The Heart: the brain can modify the rate. The brain cannot generate it.
The Lungs: seventy square meters folded into your chest, the only manual override.
beats.post: The one joystick that works, and a coach charges me ninety euros an hour to point at it.

beats.pre: My gut makes most of the calls.
beats.text: The Gut: eighty percent of the phone calls go up to the brain. The subway runs the city.
beats.post: The other twenty percent, a seminar leader sells back to me as intuition.

beats.text: The Liver: Prometheus was anatomically correct. It's the only organ that grows back.
beats.post: Which is why I treat it like it comes with a warranty. Every Friday.

beats.text: The Night Shift: sleep is the janitorial shift washing the thoughts out of the carpet.
beats.post: And every night I keep the cleaners waiting for one more episode.

beats.text: The Immune System: a library of every murder attempt. It remembers things you have forgotten.
beats.post: Every cold since kindergarten, on file. I can't remember my own passwords.

beats.text: Autoimmune: the discrimination fails, not the weapon. The gun works fine, pointed the wrong way.
beats.post: Like a company that fires the employee who reported the leak.

beats.text: Andreas Vesalius looked at the body instead of the book. Everyone else was wrong.
beats.post: Today his own faculty would cancel his talk.

beats.text: Ignaz Semmelweis saved the mothers. The doctors committed him. He died of the infection.
beats.post: Nobody wanted to hear it was their own hands.

beats.pre: We still do it, in every meeting where someone says the project is dead:
beats.text: The Semmelweis Problem: evidence available, implication uncomfortable, we reject the finding.

beats.pre: And the old quacks never retire.
beats.text: The Humoralist: wrong in the facts, right in the vibe. It was the first Kayfabe.
The Blind Eye: you have a hole in your vision. The brain fills it in with best guesses.
beats.post: Which is also how I read the news.

beats: Then I found a memo on my desk. It was about me.

beats.text: The Brain: the decision was already underway five hundred milliseconds before you made it.
You are the press secretary, not the president.

beats: So that's my job. I don't fly this thing. I explain afterwards why we meant to go there.

beats.text: The Scorekeeper: the body keeps the score because the body is the score.

beats: Now picture a whole city of us. Millions of pilots in millions of comfortable chairs, all yanking joysticks that aren't plugged in, all agreeing it's going really well. Rush hour looks exactly the same.
Thirty-two departments fit in one deck. Cut them out with a few friends, pass them round the table, and find out who runs the city at your place, and who signs everything half a second late.
revisionNote: r5b answers Georg 20.10. ('AI slop, object acting, empty phrases'): one image (pilot in a colossus), no card-art descriptions the listener cannot see, every image resolved satirically with an actor, a responsibility and an everyday reference; outro is a concrete statement about who profits. Outro per Georg 20.10.: no addressee needed; thought-provoking human-folly picture + curiosity to play the deck with friends.
